[quote=oceanice_republics;60855870][spoiler=[b]Sabrati Civil War|Twin Corridors Operations[/b]] Recap*
After the fall of the Neo-Human Fascist Party in 1946, and the establishment of the Oceanice Republic, led to the reformations of a centralized government into a republic that adopted a Hyper-Capitalist and Democratic Militarism Doctrine. Both the new government of Oceanice Republic and ULR tension increased in the early 1947 to 1948, during the standoff between Argos Straight and the dominance of the sea. What led to the first development of the Cold War in 1949, with tension peaking over power influence and trade. The first proxy war began with the Oceanice Republic's goal to support the Democratic Coalition, aiming to replace authoritarian or monarchist factions with a government aligned with Oceanics democratic-militarist doctrine.

Twin Corridors Operations

Both the Oceanice Republic & Mizrahel Support for the Democratic Coalition offer support in the civil war by the Port of Mizrahel at 03:12 Hours. A thick dust rolled off the water as the great floodlights of the Mizrahel Naval Command Pier blinked to life. The first container ship, the O.N.S. Varensh, eased alongside the reinforced dock, its hull marked only with a small Oceanice Republic code ORSAB1953/42.
Mizrahel dockworkers armed, disciplined, and moving, in a rush as the ramp lowered.

The crates began to appear. With Panzer IVs and Panthers, their turrets covered in canvas.  Two Tiger I chassis, freshly restored by Oceanice engineers.  Rows of M41 Walker Bulldogs secured with steel chains. Pallets of StG 44s, MP40s, Kar98ks, and MG42s carefully marked for the Democratic Coalition.

Commander Ravell Arsen, Mizrahel Defense Force liaison, turned to the Oceanice officer beside him
.
Commander Ravell (Mizrahel)
"Your people rebuilt half of these tanks from scrap. They look new."

Captain Veylan Strass (Oceanice Republic)
We dont give allies leftovers. We give them tools to win.

Captain Strass handed over the manifest. It was heavy.

Split Supply Operation | Twin Corridors
Route 1 | Northern Corridor, Land Border
From Mizrahels northern frontier into Democratic Coalition territory.Includes following
Halftracks of Sd.Kfz. 250 & 251, Panzer 35t and 38t light tanks, CCKW trucks
Ambulances Dodge WC-54, Mauser rifles, MGs, and Panzerfausts. Along side was fill with artillery of Nebelwerfer 42, 10.5 cm leFH, 15 cm sFH 18

Route 2 | Southern Coastal Corridor
Fast-moving naval convoys from Oceanice → Mizrahel → Democratic Coalition port cities. Includes Me 262 and Bf 109 airframes, Fw 190 and Boomerang CAS aircraft, Hummel SPGs, Wirbelwinds & Flakpanzer 38t, 8.8 cm Flak batteries, LVT-4 and LVTP-5 amphibious landing vehicles

Democratic Coalition Training Camp

Northern Sabrata Border |19:47 Hours

The desert night and the hum of engines filled the air as the Democratic Coalition recruits gathered around a new sight, with Mizraheli MSF special forces advisors and Oceanice general who used to serve back in the Post Neo-Human Regime.  Newly delivered of regime-era and early-modern armor. Captain Strass stood before a freshly assembled unit of Democratic Coalition fighters, their uniforms mismatched, but their eyes focused. Behind him, an MG42 barked into the dunes as Oceanice instructors demonstrated fire discipline.

Captain Strass (Oceanice)
You are not rebels anymore.
 You are a fighting force.
 And you will break the monarchists' rule for once!
He motioned toward a row of covered vehicles.
(Tarps lifted, revealing a Tiger II, in a desert camouflaged armor, gleaming under the lanterns. Two Panther Ausf. G units freshly painted while seven Sd.Kfz. 251s equipped for troop transport. A Nebelwerfer 42 ready for testing firing, and a line of StG 44s laid neatly on wooden tables

A Coalition officer, General Issam Daruk, stepped forward.

General Issam
This is enough to change the front.

Captain Strass:
No.
 This is enough to start changing it.
A whistle blew in the distance. The first Me 262, newly refitted and painted with Democratic Coalition markings, roared overhead on a test flight.
The Coalition fighters stared in awe.

Mizrahel Special Forces enter the scene. Mizrahel special operators emerged from the black balaclavas, suppressed rifles.

MSF Team Leader
 Dagon
We handle your raids.
 Your reconnaissance.
 Your targeting for artillery.
He pointed toward a distant Royalist outpost.
We will teach you how to strike silently.
 Oceanice will supply the firepower to strike.

Captain Strass stepped forward again, gripping Issams shoulder*

Captain Strass
The ULR and their royalists believe you are outnumbered, outgunned
 But what they dont know
 is that you now have us.

He nodded once, sharply.

Tomorrow, we begin the combined training of
 Tanks.
 Anti-air.
 Urban combat.
 Air-ground coordination.
 Night assaults with MSF support.

He looked across the desert moonlight

Captain Strass
By the end of the month, Democratic Coalition, you will not just resist. You will advance.
 And when you advance! Oceanice Republic and her allies will ensure you gain your freedom!

The recruits cheered, their voices. With Mizrahels border open, Oceanices convoys flowing, and MSF instructors on the ground, the Democratic Coalition had a focus on making them become well trained army.[/spoiler]

[b][u]Dhornaper Notices[/u][/b]

Such a large amount of support to the coalition from Oceanice and Mizrahel did not go unnoticed. Ayub Khan was notified by his Ministry of Foreign Affairs and by reading ULR and Sabrata newspapers. He did not like the meddling of Oceanice, a foreign and imperialist country, in his backyard and did not trust Mizrahel in the slightest. The war had become more serious and involved more factions that he could have imagined. Supplying resources barely above cost did not cut it for supporting the revolutionaries, who were kindred spirits in rejecting westernisation and in overthrowing a monarchy. Ayub Khan himself had overthrown his cousin, the last Shah, and himself had socialist leanings.

Ayub Khan decided to ramp up the support he was offering. He would stop charging for the resources needed and would offer the revolutionaries sanctuary in Dhornaper for their factories, for training their soldiers, and for their leadership. He would also ramp up oil production to finance small arms and vehicle development vehicle and manufacturing, both for domestic industrial capacity and for the rebels. Dhornaper would need Sabratan help to build native expertise but the Sabratans would be unlikely to refuse his offer.

[/spoiler]

[spoiler=[b]Negotiations win, budgets fail[/b]]
The convoy would arrive in the dead of night at a port on the western coast of Durani. This convoy of Hydronian military ships had traveled from a port in Turqevia, through the Argos strait and towards Sabrata, carefully avoiding the waters of Dhornaper and Sabratan territory that was not held by the Democratic coalition. Unusual amounts of precaution would be taken for this convoys journey to ensure that its package reached Sabrata in one piece, although it would be foolish for any nation to attack a Hydronian diplomatic vessel, especially one carrying such a prestigious passenger; President Halil Ozhid of Hydronia.

Upon arrival, several high-ranking military personnel would step out to greet the Sabratans first, whilst scouts with binoculars would survey the landscape around them. Halil had to be sure that it was safe for him to engage in these negotiations, Sabrata was engaged in civil war afterall, it was hardly the safest location to engage in negotiations. Nevertheless, Halil had agreed to make the somewhat perilous journey despite his better judgment, these negotiations had to succeed at all costs, or it would ruin Hydronias internal and international reputation, not to mention the fact that Hydronia needed to secure its interests in the Argos strait, which began with regime change in Sabrata.

Once the situation had been declared safe for Halil to involve himself in, he would make his formal appearance, waking out of the vessel to greet the Sabratan dignitaries present whilst Hydronian soldiers stood tall and saluted. Once the formalities had been completed, the real negotiations would begin. Hydronia would set forward the following points for cooperation:
[list]
[*]Hydronia will be allowed access to a Sabratan airbase on the island of Durani, for sole use in aerial operations across Sabrata
[*]Hydronian companies will be allowed to extract Sabratan natural resources from the island of Durani
[*]Hydronia will continue to carry out nightly airstrikes against enemy factions in the civil war
[*]Hydronia will begin arms and armoured vehicle shipments to the Democratic Coalition
[/list]
Hydronia awaits confirmation from the Democratic Coalition.

Once an agreement with the Democratic Coalition could be reached, the diplomatic convoy would leave Sabratan waters swiftly, heading back through the Argos Strait and towards a port in Nordiheim. The central Argossian nation had been identified as a potentially priceless ally to Hydronia, despite the rocky history between the two nations. Whilst Hydronia had no solid offers or terms for Negotiations with Nordiheim, Halil would certainly have his eyes set upon some diplomatic objectives.

Upon arrival in Nordiheim, Halil would make his exit immediately, both due to the lack of danger in Nordiheim that was present in Sabrata and as a show of trust to his Argossian counterparts. Once again, formalities would commence, but they would not be as swift. Hydronias objectives in Nordiheim were different to with Sabrata. Instead of aiming to secure a deal as quickly as possible, Halil would aim to slowly build up trust and improve bilateral relations with Nordiheim.

Once the formalities were once again over and done with, the Hydronian delegation would set out a potential plan for cooperation with Nordiheim in the Sabratan civil war. The plan would consist of naval cooperation between the two nations to secure the Argos strait and to protect the naval interests of the Democratic Coalition. Additionally, Hydronia would make request for a possible deal to acquire potential temporary rights to operate in a Nordiheimian airbase to improve the effectiveness and efficiency of Hydronian bombing operations across hostile factions in Sabrata. Halil would offer a sizeable monetary payment if Nordiheim would allow Hydronia to use its airbase.

Whilst Hydronian successes would only continue to grow abroad, back at home there would be much dismay. In the parliamentary assembly, the opposition would heavily criticise Halils increasing military spending, citing the impacts it is having and will further have on the Hydronian economy. Whilst no one could deny that Hydronia was doing a good job of asserting its influence across the globe, especially given the tumultuous era that Erene was living through, the Social Unity Party would accuse the government of putting the civilians of other nations, Sabrata in particular, before their own. Spending in Sabrata had soared as a result of new military programs, aid-lending deals and heavy bombing, and many in the opposition believed that it would simply not be sustainable.

For now, Halil would not Manke any adjustments to the budget, believing that the economy would soon recover as the people acclimatised to the future, but this would only further anger the opposition, creating a clear divide on the matter between Hydronias politicians.

[i]Will Halils decisions be the right ones? Only time will tell[/i]
[/spoiler]
